cities.d: capital and largest city in the country

x.around: Motos are plentiful throughout the capital, and a good distance on a moto will cost you CFA 300. Taxis can be rented from around CFA 500, with CFA 2000 getting you basically anywhere in town. There are route taxis, costing normally CFA 200-400, but if you are visiting they are difficult to figure out and only ever really used by local folks.
x.intro: Lomé is the capital and largest city of Togo. With a population of almost 2.2 million (2023), the city is the economic and cultural center of the country. Around a quarter of the country's population lives here.
x.safe: The beaches and surrounding areas are known for frequent muggings, especially at night. Don’t wander around on your own at night on the beach unless there are plenty of people around.

cities.d: previously known as Anecho, it is a town in southeastern Togo, lying on the Gulf of Guinea near the border of Benin

x.intro: Aného is a town of 25,000 people (2010) in southeastern Togo on the Gulf of Guinea near the border of Benin. Aného is an old German colonial town, and a centre of voodoo along the West African pilgrimage route Voodoo Trail, which connects Lomé with Ouagadougou in Burkina Faso.

hidden.d: A 100-m waterfall rushing down a granite cliff into a pool deep in the forest. The waterfall is at the end of a 40-minute hike along narrow paths that wind through hillside cocoa plantations before entering the forest.

x.intro: Badou is a town of 24,000 people nestled in the Akposso mountains, in the West Plateau Region. Badou is the capital and the main market of the district of Wawa, a border region specialized in the production of cocoa.

next.d: border is about 10 km from the city with several official border crossings.

must.d: The French colonists built the impressive chateau in 1940. Since then however, the humid climate and sporadic maintenance of Chataeu Vial has led to it deteriorating.

intro: Togo is a narrow country in West Africa, sandwiched between Ghana on the west and Benin on the east. It is a charming country, mostly due to its charming people as there are not many tourist attractions. Wedged in its skinny size, Togo boasts a deep spiritual heritage and striking sun-drenched landscapes.

other.d: a UNESCO world heritage site where the traditional Batammariba people live in mud tower-houses

x.around: Because the traditional mud fortresses are scattered loosely across farmland, forests, and valleys rather than packed into dense urban blocks, walking on foot along marked village trails is mandatory. Local motorcycle taxis can be chartered for the day to bridge the distances between the primary distributed clan communities.

hidden.d: The main social and economic hub for the Batammariba people. Once a week, locals from scattered mountain valley settlements gather to trade fresh sorghum, hand-carved pipes, traditional pottery, and specialized headpieces…

x.intro: Koutammakou (Batammariba Country) is a cultural landscape in Northern Togo along its border with Benin. This guide focuses on the Togo side, known for its traditional mud tower-houses (takienta) and rich cultural heritage.

next.d: . The closest large town and the third-largest city in Togo, acting as a base for banking, comfortable hotels, and reliable internet connections.

other.d: a town known for its Friday market which has one of the largest voodoo markets in West Africa

x.around: A taxi-moto (motorcycle taxi) will cost CFA 150-500 to get you around. You can tell who the taxi-moto drivers are: they will honk or hiss at you as they drive by and usually wear baseball caps and sunglasses. A taxi will usually cost about CFA 500 for a one-way short trip inside the city, for trips to the northern parts of the city expect to pay up to CFA 2,500.
x.intro: Togo is a narrow country in West Africa, sandwiched between Ghana on the west and Benin on the east. It is a charming country, mostly due to its charming people as there are not many tourist attractions. Wedged in its skinny size, Togo boasts a deep spiritual heritage and striking sun-drenched landscapes.
x.safe: As a rule, stay away from public beaches, where tourists find themselves mugged any time of day or night. Most of the country has little crime, but Lomé is a clear exception, and is a good deal more dangerous than any city in Ghana or Benin. If going somewhere at night, take a car taxi, and get the numbers of a few trusted taxi drivers if you plan to stay for a while.
